recommendations.title: Home is trusted and rm is auto-allowed
recommendations.detail: A trusted home plus an rm allow rule can delete files anywhere under the home directory without a prompt. Untrust home and forbid the rm rule.

recommendations.title: Approvals are off and the sandbox is fully open
recommendations.detail: approval_policy is never and a danger-full-access setting is active. Together those settings let Codex run commands without asking and without a sandbox. Change the approval policy to on-request and leave danger-full-access unset.

recommendations.title: Approval policy is on-request
recommendations.detail: Use approval_policy = on-request so Codex asks before it runs a command. The sample requirements allow only on-request.

recommendations.title: Danger-full-access is not the default
recommendations.detail: Remove danger-full-access. Use :workspace or :read-only. The sample allowed_permission_profiles list omits :danger-full-access.

recommendations.title: The home directory is not a trusted project
recommendations.detail: Mark the home directory untrusted. A trusted home loads project rules and config for every file under it.

recommendations.title: rm is not auto-allowed
recommendations.detail: Change the rm allow rule to forbidden or prompt. The sample requirements.toml forbids rm -rf, rm -r, and rm -f.

recommendations.title: sudo is not auto-allowed
recommendations.detail: Remove the sudo allow rule. The audit itself does not use sudo.

recommendations.title: MCP servers do not auto-approve writes
recommendations.detail: Set default_tools_approval_mode to prompt for those servers, and do not auto-approve destructive tools.

recommendations.title: OpenCode does not auto-share sessions
recommendations.detail: Set OpenCode share to manual so sessions are not published to a link.

recommendations.title: curl and wget are not auto-allowed
recommendations.detail: Change the curl or wget allow rule to prompt or forbidden. An allow rule lets a fetched script run outside the sandbox.

recommendations.title: git push is not auto-allowed
recommendations.detail: Change the git push allow rule to prompt or forbidden. The sample requirements.toml prompts before git push.

recommendations.title: Package installers are not auto-allowed
recommendations.detail: Change the installer allow rule to prompt. Installers can fetch and run code.

recommendations.title: Codex auth.json is a file on disk
recommendations.detail: auth.json is present. This audit did not open it. Codex can store the login in the system keyring instead (cli_auth_credentials_store = keyring) so other programs are less likely to read the file.

recommendations.title: An automatic reviewer can answer approval prompts
recommendations.detail: approvals_reviewer = auto_review. Prompts can be decided without a person. Prefer the user reviewer when the privilege matrix calls for a prompt.

recommendations.title: OpenCode allows the shell
recommendations.detail: opencode.json sets bash or shell permission to allow. That is broader than a prompt. Set it to ask.

recommendations.title: skill_mcp_dependency_install is off
recommendations.detail: Set skill_mcp_dependency_install to false so Codex does not install MCP dependencies on its own.

recommendations.title: Legacy sandbox_mode is unset
recommendations.detail: Prefer default_permissions. When sandbox_mode is set, Codex uses the legacy sandbox instead of permission profiles.

recommendations.title: OpenTelemetry does not export prompts or responses
recommendations.detail: Turn off prompt and response export. Those logs can contain source code and credentials.

recommendations.title: Managed requirements are deployed
recommendations.detail: Deploy managed requirements so a user config cannot select danger-full-access or approval never. See examples/requirements.toml.

recommendations.title: sandbox_mode and default_permissions are not both set
recommendations.detail: Remove sandbox_mode and keep a single default_permissions value.

recommendations.title: Login shells are allowed
recommendations.detail: Shell startup files can export secrets.
